summary: Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned an MA at McMaster University, studying under supervisor James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown (~1960–1964) and became Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA (~1969–1994).

Kei Kataoka (b. 1969), an Indologist and philosopher, studied at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University. He held positions at Wolfson College, Oxford, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University, where he serves as professor (attested 2026).
Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University and serves on its faculty (attested 2026).

Keiichi Miyamoto (b. 1948) is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He worked at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute before serving as lecturer, associate professor, and professor at Kokugakuin University.
Keiji Iwata (1922–2013) worked in religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1943–1947) and held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1973–1980) and Otani University.
Keiji Kokubu (1907–1997) was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He later held posts at Ryukoku University, Nanzan University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Hajime Tanabe, and at Freiburg under Martin Heidegger, he taught at Otani University before becoming a professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964).

Keiki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at and held a post at Kyoto University. Nakayama also held posts at JSPS (attested 2020) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He taught at Shukyo University, served as associate professor at Tokyo, and was a professor at Taisho University (~1926–1939).
Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).
Keinin Hayashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a lecturer at Waseda University and as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned a PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham (~2007–2011). Strickland held posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Koyasan University (1959–1973, 2005–2009) and Kochi University (~1968–1995), where he was a professor.

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor at Rissho University (~1965–1980) and Tohoku University (~1980–1993), and later served as president of Hosen Gakuen College.

Keisuke Fujii (b. 1953) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in engineering at the University of Tokyo and served there from 1982 to 2018 as assistant, associate professor, and professor.

Keith Dowman (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under numerous traditional teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi (b. 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He has held teaching and leadership positions at Shuchiin University and Taisho University.

Kelsang Gyatso (1931–2022) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and philosopher. Educated at monasteries including Sera, where he earned a Geshe degree, he taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre beginning in 1977 and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Kelsey Alise Seymour is a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who completed a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and was a visiting predoctoral fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).
